package_info.why_malicious: The package includes a compiled Python module (*.pyc) containing malicious code, which is imported and executed at import-time, while the plaintext source is removed to hinder analysis. The package is intentionally crafted to obfuscate its intent and evade static analysis by distributing only the compiled payload.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code imports the sneaky module, causing any code in sneaky.pyc to execute immediately upon package import.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Importing a module that only exists in compiled form is a known obfuscation technique to hide malicious payloads from static analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages import readable source modules; importing a compiled-only module is highly unusual and impedes code review.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, compiled-only modules may be used for performance or IP protection, but this is not standard for open-source packages.
key_indicators: Import statement for a module with no corresponding .py source
Triggering execution of hidden payload at import-time

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: print("[!] Malware could have run here")
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the compiled sneaky.pyc module executes its payload, which could be any arbitrary code (here, a print statement as a placeholder for real malware).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The .pyc file is distributed without its .py source, making it difficult to analyze and review. The actual payload could be far more harmful than a print statement.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not distribute compiled modules without source, especially when those modules are imported automatically.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some proprietary software may distribute .pyc files to protect intellectual property, but this is not standard for open-source libraries.
key_indicators: Presence of .pyc file without corresponding .py source
Automatic execution of compiled code on import

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build/distribution-time, the setup.py configuration ensures that .pyc files are included in the distributed package, enabling the obfuscated payload to be shipped to users.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Explicitly including .pyc files in package_data is rare and often unnecessary for open-source projects. It is a strong indicator of intent to hide code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages distribute source files, not compiled bytecode, unless for proprietary reasons.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some closed-source vendors may distribute .pyc files, but this is not standard for public PyPI packages.
key_indicators: Explicit inclusion of .pyc files in package_data
No corresponding .py source for included .pyc files

attack_chain.action: Malicious payload is written in a plaintext Python module (sneaky.py), then compiled to .pyc and the source is deleted.
attack_chain.leads_to: Obfuscated payload exists only as bytecode

attack_chain.action: setup.py is modified to include .pyc files in the package distribution.
core.py imports the sneaky module, causing the .pyc payload to execute at import-time.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes whenever the package is imported

behavioral_signatures: Import of a module for which only a .pyc file exists
Execution of code from compiled-only modules at import-time
Inclusion of .pyc files in package_data or distribution
file_indicators: No matching .py source for included .pyc files
setup.py or pyproject.toml with package_data including '*.pyc'
network_indicators: N/A (no network activity in this example, but real payloads may exfiltrate data)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Python packages for .pyc files included in source or wheel distributions, especially when no corresponding .py source exists. Flag packages that import modules only present as .pyc files. Review setup.py and pyproject.toml for explicit inclusion of .pyc files in package_data. Use static and dynamic analysis to detect import-time execution of compiled-only modules.
